examples.title: Compose two proof steps
examples.scope: This checks composition of explicit hypotheses, not the truth of either hypothesis.
examples.code:
import Std

-- Each hypothesis is explicit: this proves the composition, not P itself.
theorem compose_steps (P Q R : Prop)
    (first : P → Q) (second : Q → R) : P → R := by
  intro proofOfP
  have proofOfQ : Q := first proofOfP
  exact second proofOfQ

examples.title: A finite valuation implies nonzero
examples.scope: Uses an abstract Option-valued model. The finite-valuation hypothesis is supplied, not proved for a research determinant.
examples.code:
import Std

-- none models an infinite valuation; some k models a finite valuation.
-- Establishing the hypothesis finiteVal for a determinant is separate work.
theorem nonzero_of_finite_value {α : Type} (zero : α)
    (valuation : α → Option Int) (atZero : valuation zero = none)
    (q : α) (k : Int) (finiteVal : valuation q = some k) : q ≠ zero := by
  intro equalsZero
  rw [equalsZero, atZero] at finiteVal
  contradiction

examples.title: The finite-sum formula by induction
examples.scope: Checks the exact natural-number identity 2·sumTo n=n(n+1), including n=0.
examples.code:
import Std

def sumTo : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 => sumTo n + (n + 1)

-- Twice the sum avoids division in natural numbers.
theorem twice_sum (n : Nat) : 2 * sumTo n = n * (n + 1) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ n ih =>
    simp only [sumTo, Nat.mul_add, Nat.add_mul, Nat.mul_one, Nat.one_mul] at *
    omega

#print axioms twice_sum
examples.compilerOutput: 'twice_sum' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]

examples.title: Reuse a lemma in two proofs
examples.scope: An elementary example of two results sharing the same proved prerequisite.
examples.code:
import Std

-- A named lemma can support more than one result.
theorem positive_implies_nonzero (n : Nat) (h : 0 < n) : n ≠ 0 := by
  omega

theorem successor_nonzero (n : Nat) : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by
  apply positive_implies_nonzero
  omega

theorem square_positive_input_nonzero (n : Nat) (h : 0 < n) : n * n ≠ 0 := by
  exact Nat.mul_ne_zero (positive_implies_nonzero n h) (positive_implies_nonzero n h)

#print axioms successor_nonzero
#print axioms square_positive_input_nonzero
examples.compilerOutput:
'successor_nonzero' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]
'square_positive_input_nonzero' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]

examples.title: A finite sum splits over concatenation
examples.scope: A recursive natural-number list sum, proved by structural induction.

def total : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | x :: xs => x + total xs

theorem result (xs ys : List Nat) : total (xs ++ ys) = total xs + total ys := by
  induction xs with
  | nil => simp [total]
  | cons x xs ih => simp [total, ih, Nat.add_assoc]

examples.title: Finite graph paths concatenate
examples.scope: A graph is an arbitrary relation; reachability is its inductively defined reflexive-transitive closure.
examples.code:
import Std

inductive Reach {α : Type} (edge : α → α → Prop) : α → α → Prop where
  | refl (a) : Reach edge a a
  | step {a b c} : edge a b → Reach edge b c → Reach edge a c

theorem result {α : Type} {edge : α → α → Prop} {a b c : α}
    (ab : Reach edge a b) (bc : Reach edge b c) : Reach edge a c := by
  induction ab with
  | refl => exact bc
  | step e path ih => exact Reach.step e (ih bc)
